### Summary

The paper studies the sparse learning and uncertainty quantification of deep neural networks (DNNs) via the newly proposed stochastic neural network (StoNet). StoNet is a probabilistic model, where the neurons in the hidden layers are assumed to be stochastic and the weights are modeled as Gaussian distributions. The authors show that the sparse learning theory and methods developed for linear models can be adapted to DNNs via StoNet. They also propose a recursive method to quantify the prediction uncertainty for the StoNet. The authors conduct numerical experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of StoNet.
